questions.q:
Statement-I: Unit chosen for measuring physical quantities should not be accessible.
Statement-II: Unit should change with the changing physical conditions like temperature, pressure, etc.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are incorrect.
Statement-I is correct & Statement-II is incorrect.
Statement-I is incorrect & Statement-II is correct.
questions.solution:
Statement-I:
"Unit chosen for measuring physical quantities should not be accessible."
This is wrong. Units must be accessible and reproducible, so that measurements are standardized.
Statement-II:
"Unit should change with the changing physical conditions like temperature, pressure, etc."
This is also wrong. Units must be constant and not vary with physical conditions.
Correct Answer: (2) Both Statement-I and Statement-II are incorrect.

Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

The unit of energy per unit volume is,

Jm3=J m-3 means, kg m-1 s-2 and the unit of angular momentum, mvr=kg m2 s-1 are not same so they can not be added, so we can say that same unit quantities can be added and subtracted and same unit quantities have same dimension.

Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.solution:
Viscous force is given by F=ηAdvdt, here, A is area and dvdt is velocity gradient.

Thus, η=FAdvdt.

Now, Pt=FAt=ηdvdtt

Then, Pt=ML-1T-1=η

Thus, assertion is true but reason is false.

Both Statement-I and Statement-II are incorrect.

questions.solution: The specific gravity or relative density is defined as the ratio of the density of the substance to the density of water at \(4^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\). Since specific gravity is a pure ratio, it has no unit and hence, no dimensions.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and other is labelled as Reason (R)

Assertion (A) : Time period of oscillation of a liquid drop depends on surface tension S, if density of the liquid is ρ and radius of the drop is r, then T=Kρr3S32 is dimensionally correct, where K is dimensionless.

Reason (R) : Using dimensional analysis we get R.H.S. having different dimension than that of time period. In the light of above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Using dimensional analysis for the given equation,

T=Kρr3S32

⇒K=TS34ρ12r32⇒K=TM34T-32M12L-32L32⇒K=M14T-12

Therefore, K is not dimensionless. Hence, Assertion is false.

For dimensional validity of the given equation, K can not be dimensionless. If it is dimensionless then

Dimensions of L.H.S ≠ Dimensions of R.H.S

∴ Option (D) is correct.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Mass, volume and time may be taken as fundamental quantities in a system of units.
Reason (R): Mass, volume and time are independent of one another.
options: Assertion (A) is true, Reason (R) is true; Reason (R) is a correct explanation for Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, Reason (R) is true; Reason (R) is not a correct explanation for Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A):
"Mass, volume and time may be taken as fundamental quantities in a system of units."
This is false, because volume is a derived quantity (volume \(=\) length \({ }^3\)). Fundamental quantities are like mass, length, time, etc.
Reason (R):
"Mass, volume and time are independent of one another."
This is true, because mass, volume, and time are indeed independent physical quantities (though volume is derived, it is still independent of mass and time).
Correct Answer: (4) Assertion (A) is false, Reason (R) is true.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Special functions such as trigonometric, logarithmic and exponential functions are not dimensionless.
Reason (R): A pure number, ratio of similar physical quantities, such as angle and refractive index, has no dimensions.
options: Assertion (A) is true, Reason (R) is true; Reason (R) is a correct explanation for Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, Reason (R) is true; Reason (R) is not a correct explanation for Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
The arguments of special functions, such as the trigonometric, logarithmic and exponential functions must be dimensionless.
A pure number, ratio of similar physical quantities, such as angle as the ratio (length/length), refractive index as the ratio of (speed of light in vacuum/speed of light in medium), etc. has no dimensions.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): When we change the unit of measurement of a quantity, its numerical value changes.
Reason (R): Smaller the unit of measurement smaller is its numerical value.
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct and statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect and statement II is correct.
Both statements I and statements II are incorrect.
questions.solution:
If \(u_1\) and \(u_2\) be the units to measure a quantity Q and \(n_1\) and \(n_2\) be the numerical values respectively then we know that \(Q=n_1 u_1=n_2 u_2\).
Since the quantity \(Q\) does not change irrespective of the units used to measure it \(Q=\) constant.
So nu \(=\) constant \(\Rightarrow n \propto \frac{1}{u}\) i.e., smaller the unit of measurement, greater is the corresponding numerical value.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): If \(x\) and \(y\) are the distance along \(x\) and \(y\) axes respectively then the dimensions of \(\frac{d^3 y}{d x^3}\) is \(\mathrm{M}^0 \mathrm{~L}^{-2} \mathrm{~T}^0\).
Reason (R): Dimensions of \(\int_a^b y d x\) is \(\mathrm{M}^0 \mathrm{~L}^2 \mathrm{~T}^0\).
options: Assertion (A) is true, Reason (R) is truc; Reason (R) is a correct explanation for Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is truc, Reason (R) is truc; Reason (R) is not a correct explanation for Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is falsc, Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A):
"If \(x\) and \(y\) are distances along \(x\) and \(y\) axes respectively, then the dimensions of \(\frac{d^3 y}{d x^3}\) is \(M^0 L^{-2} T^{0 . "}\)
- Here, \(y\) has dimensions of length (L).
- \(x\) also has dimensions of length (L).
- Differentiating once: \(\frac{d y}{d x} \rightarrow L / L=\) dimensionless.
- Differentiating twice: \(\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2} \rightarrow\) dimension \(=1 / L\).
- Differentiating thrice: \(\frac{d^3 y}{d x^3} \rightarrow\) dimension \(=1 / L^2=L^{-2}\).
So, dimensions = \(M^0 L^{-2} T^0\).
(1) Assertion (A) is true.

Names of units of some physical quantities are given in List-I and their dimensions formulae are given in List-Il. Match the correct pairs in the lists $\begin{array}{ll|ll}

$\begin{array}{llll}A & B & C & D\end{array}

Some physical constants are given in List-I and their dimensional formulae are given in List-II. Match the following

The correct answer is
questions.solution:
(1) Planck's constant
$\begin{aligned} {[h] } & =\left[\frac{E}{v}\right] \\ & =\frac{\left[\mathrm{ML}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]}{\left[\mathrm{T}^{-1}\right]}=\left[\mathrm{ML}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-1}\right]\end{aligned}$
(2) Gravitational constant
$\begin{aligned} {[G] } & =\left[\frac{F r^2}{m_1 m_2}\right] \\ & =\frac{\left[\mathrm{MLT}^{-2}\right]\left[\mathrm{L}^2\right]}{\left[\mathrm{M}^2\right]} \\ & =\left[\mathrm{M}^{-1} \mathrm{~L}^3 \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]\end{aligned}$
(3) Bulk modulus
$\begin{aligned} {[B] } & =\frac{[\text { Normal stress }]}{[\text { Volumetric strain }]} \\ & =\left[\mathrm{ML}^{-1} \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]\end{aligned}$
(4) Coefficient of viscosity,
$\begin{aligned} \eta & =\frac{[F]}{[A][d v / d y]}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{ML}^{-2}\right][\mathrm{L}]}{\left[\mathrm{L}^2\right]\left[\mathrm{LT}^{-1}\right]} \\ & =\left[\mathrm{ML}^{-1} \mathrm{~T}^{-1}\right]\end{aligned}$
Hence, option (d) is correct.

Names of units of some physical quantities are given in List-I, and their corresponding dimensional formulae are given in List-II. Match the correct pairs.
\(\begin{array}{l|l}
\text { List-I (Physical Quantities) } & \text { List-II (Dimensional Formulae) } \\
\hline \text { (A) Surface Tension } & \text { (i) }\left[M L^2 T^{-1}\right] \\
\text { (B) Planck's Constant } & \text { (ii) }\left[M L^{0} T^{-2}\right] \\
\text { (C) Boltzmann Constant } & \text { (iii) }\left[M L^2 T^{-2} K^{-1}\right] \\
\text { (D) Magnetic Flux } & \text { (iv) }\left[M L^2 T^{-2} A^{-1}\right]
\end{array}\)
questions.solution:
- Surface Tension \(\rightarrow\) (ii) \(\left[M L^{0} T^{-2}\right]\)
- Planck's Constant \(\rightarrow\) (i) \(\left[M L^2 T^{-1}\right]\)
- Boltzmann Constant \(\rightarrow\) (iii) \(\left[M L^2 T^{-2} K^{-1}\right]\)
- Magnetic Flux \(\rightarrow\) (iv) \(\left[M L^2 T^{-2} A^{-1}\right]\)
